claims.quote: Kerley B lines CXR Interstitial pulmonary edema (CHF)

claims.text: Cardiomegaly: cardiac silhouette > 50% of the thoracic cage on a PA film; cephalization: upper lobe pulmonary vessels become more prominent; both are often seen in heart failure
claims.quote: This patient has cardiomegaly (width of cardiac silhouette is > 50% of thoracic cage on a posterior-anterior chest radiograph). The patient also has cephalization (black arrows) whereby upper lobe pulmonary vessels become more prominent. These findings are often seen in patients with heart failure.

claims.text: Kerley B lines: horizontal lines in the lung periphery that extend to the pleural surface; they denote thickened, edematous interlobular septa, often due to pulmonary edema
claims.quote: Kerley B lines (arrows) are horizontal lines in the lung periphery that extend to the pleural surface. They denote thickened, edematous interlobular septa often due to pulmonary edema.

claims.text: Bat-wing / butterfly: bilateral perihilar patchy opacities consistent with cardiogenic pulmonary edema
claims.quote: This radiograph shows bilateral perihilar patchy opacities in a "bat-wing" or "butterfly" pattern consistent with cardiogenic pulmonary edema.
claims.locator: Chest Radiograph of a Patient with Pulmonary Edema (image caption)

claims.text: Other heart failure findings: enlarged cardiac silhouette, pleural effusion, fluid in the major fissure and Kerley B lines, reflecting chronic left atrial pressure elevation and septal edema; upper lobe venous congestion and interstitial or alveolar edema may also be present
claims.quote: Chest radiograph findings suggesting heart failure include an enlarged cardiac silhouette, pleural effusion, fluid in the major fissure, and horizontal lines in the periphery of lower posterior lung fields (Kerley B lines). These findings reflect chronic elevation of left atrial pressure and chronic thickening of the intralobular septa due to edema. Upper lobe pulmonary venous congestion and interstitial or alveolar edema may also be present.

claims.text: Thoracic ultrasound: the "comet tail artifact" corresponds to Kerley B lines
claims.quote: Sonographic "comet tail artifact" on thoracic ultrasound corresponds to the radiographic finding of Kerley B lines.

claims.text: Lung US (her chart): ≥3 B-lines per field → pulmonary edema (cardiogenic) / interstitial process
claims.quote: ≥3 B-lines per field (lung US) Pulmonary edema (cardiogenic) / interstitial process
claims.locator: Non-Trauma Ultrasound Findings, Lung / Cardiac POCUS table

claims.text: Causes Cardiogenic pulmonary edema: acute alveolar flooding caused by pulmonary venous hypertension secondary to severe left ventricular failure
claims.quote: Cardiogenic pulmonary edema is acute alveolar flooding caused by pulmonary venous hypertension secondary to severe left ventricular failure.

claims.text: Triggers: acute coronary ischemia, decompensated heart failure, arrhythmia, an acute valvular disorder or acute volume overload
claims.quote: Acute pulmonary edema can result from acute coronary ischemia, decompensation of underlying heart failure, arrhythmia, an acute valvular disorder, or acute volume overload.

claims.text: Symptoms Severe dyspnea, diaphoresis, wheezing and sometimes blood-tinged frothy sputum
claims.quote: Patients have severe dyspnea, diaphoresis, wheezing, and sometimes blood-tinged frothy sputum.

claims.text: Heart failure clues (usually not apparent early): exertional dyspnea or fatigue, orthopnea, edema, tachycardia, pulmonary crackles, S3, jugular venous distention
claims.quote: Clinical findings (eg, exertional dyspnea or fatigue, orthopnea, edema, tachycardia, pulmonary crackles, S3, jugular venous distention) suggest heart failure but are usually not apparent early.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: diuresis; echo to characterize HFrEF vs HFpEF
claims.quote: Diuresis; echo to characterize HFrEF vs HFpEF
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Cardiac / Vascular / PE table

claims.text: Treat the cause and give oxygen and IV furosemide and/or nitrates as needed; inotropic agents to increase cardiac output; try noninvasive ventilatory assistance first, tracheal intubation if necessary
claims.quote: Treat the cause and give oxygen and IV furosemide and/or nitrates as needed; inotropic agents to increase cardiac output, try noninvasive ventilatory assistance initially but use tracheal intubation and assisted ventilation if necessary.

claims.text: Workup: chest radiograph, ECG, BNP, echocardiography and further testing as needed
claims.quote: Perform chest radiograph, ECG, brain (B-type) natriuretic peptide levels, echocardiography, and additional testing as necessary.
